title: 3I/ATLAS: A Cosmic Visitor from Beyond Our Solar System
author: Dad
excerpt: Comet 3I/ATLAS is the third known object from outside our solar system to be discovered passing through our celestial neighborhood. Astronomers have categorized this object as interstellar because of the hyperbolic shape of its orbital path.
content:
Meet 3I/ATLAS, an extraordinary comet that's visiting our solar system from another star system! Discovered in July 2025, it's only the third known interstellar object to pass through our cosmic neighborhood.

On October 3, 2025, 3I/ATLAS made its closest approach to Mars, coming within 18 million miles (29 million kilometers) of the Red Planet. Traveling at a staggering speed of 130,000 mph (209,000 km/h), the comet was observed by various spacecraft, including NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA's Mars Express. These observations provided scientists with valuable data about the comet's composition and behavior.

Despite its impressive size—estimated to be over 5 kilometers in diameter and weighing around 33 billion tons—3I/ATLAS poses no threat to Earth. It is expected to pass by our planet in December 2025 at a safe distance of approximately 167 million miles (269 million kilometers).

Scientists are particularly interested in studying 3I/ATLAS because of its unusual composition. Unlike typical comets from our solar system, which are primarily composed of water ice, 3I/ATLAS contains a significant amount of carbon dioxide. This discovery could provide new insights into the chemical makeup of distant star systems and the materials that form comets.

As 3I/ATLAS continues its journey through our solar system, astronomers around the world are closely monitoring its path. Upcoming observations by the European Space Agency's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE) mission, which is en route to Jupiter, will further enhance our understanding of this remarkable interstellar visitor.

Stay tuned for more updates as 3I/ATLAS continues to captivate the scientific community and skywatchers alike!
